newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 26.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* The market will continue to consolidate ahead of the Hong Kong handover, the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting on interest rates and the Dow's overnight drop, Asiamerit Securities senior investment analyst Ramon Saulo said.

* Volume will be light in the coming days as investors await Hong Kong's handover to China and the release of second quarter earnings results, said Jidgette Valenzuela, research manager at Lippo Securities.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed 11.02 points up at 2,829.29 points.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 68.08 points lower at 7,689.98. PLDT's ADR closed up $0/05 at $62/13.
* The Philippine peso closed unchanged at 26.374 to the dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 15.0625 percent.

* The Philippines failed to attract buyers for the Food Terminal Inc, a sprawling agro-industrial complex, in a bidding on Wednesday, as fears of a property glut discouraged prospective bidders, officials and local executives said.

* A Reuters poll of seven stock brokerages showed that ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp is expected to post a 22 percent rise in net income to 824 million pesos in the first six months ending June as it recovers from a row with advertisers.
* The Philippines will maintain tariffs on sugar imports from Southeast Asian countries at 65 percent starting July 1 up to 1998, President Ramos said in an executive order.
* Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc has set the offer price for its one-for-three rights issue at 2.67 pesos per share.
* Benguet Corp said it would suspend operations at its Dizon copper-gold mines starting August 1 because of damage caused by a typhoon in the last week of May.

* State-owned National Development Corp said its board approved the acquisition by construction firm DMCI Holdings Inc of a 69 percent equity stake in the country's biggest coal supplier, Semirara Coal Corp from Voest Alpine Machinery Construction & Engineering GmbH, a unit of VA Technologies AG.
* The Philippine current account deficit in the first three months of the year widened to $1.13 billion from the year-ago level of $923 million, the Central Bank reported.

* Times Journal said gaming firm Belle Corp is raising 10.319 billion pesos with the issuance of its shares via private placement and warrants, the company told the Securities and Exchange Commission.
